standard.title: Choose metric units
standard.description: Choose appropriate metric units when measuring the length, mass and capacity of objects; use smaller units or a combination of units to obtain a more accurate measure
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can measure with scaled instruments using formal units (AC9M4M01). They have not yet selected the most appropriate metric unit for a given measurement or combined units for greater accuracy.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students choose appropriate metric units for length, mass and capacity and use smaller units or combinations of units for greater accuracy.

nodes.label: Metric unit relationships
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can state the relationship between common metric units and explain which is larger or smaller.
nodes.minimum_width: State the relationship between at least two metric units for one attribute (e.g. 1 m = 100 cm = 1000 mm); order metric units from largest to smallest.
nodes.typical_width: Identify and describe unit relationships for length (mm, cm, m, km), mass (g, kg, t) and capacity (mL, L); explain the 10/100/1000 relationship patterns.
wider: Connect metric prefixes to their meanings (milli-, centi-, kilo-)
Explore non-SI units still in common use and compare to metric equivalents

response_modes.reason: Unit relationship knowledge is foundational for appropriate unit selection and conversion. Students need fluency before they can make principled choices.

nodes.hinge_reason: Unit relationship fluency is required by Node 2 — students who cannot reliably state metric relationships cannot justify why one unit is more appropriate than another for a given measurement.
success_criteria: Student correctly states the relationship between two given metric units
Student orders metric units for a given attribute from smallest to largest

nodes.label: Choosing appropriate units
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select the most appropriate metric unit for a given measurement task and justify their choice.
nodes.minimum_width: Select an appropriate unit for a given measurement (e.g. mm for pencil width, km for road distance) and justify the choice.
nodes.typical_width: Apply unit selection across length, mass and capacity contexts; compare the appropriateness of multiple units for a single measurement; explain the trade-off between precision and convenience.
wider: Survey how different professions (nurses, builders, scientists) select units in practice
Investigate First Nations measurement practices and compare to metric system conventions

response_modes.reason: Appropriate unit selection is context-dependent. Students who see only table-drill exercises over-apply one unit. Varied real contexts build the judgement to select rather than recall.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Professional contexts and cross-cultural measurement practices give advancing students rich comparative material.
success_criteria: Student selects an appropriate unit for a given context
Student explains why the chosen unit is more appropriate than an alternative

nodes.label: Combining units for accuracy
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use a combination of metric units to express a measurement more accurately than a single unit allows.
nodes.minimum_width: Express a measurement using two units (e.g. 1 m 34 cm); explain why the combination is more accurate than either unit alone.
nodes.typical_width: Measure and record length, mass and capacity using combinations of units; convert between combined and single-unit expressions; compare precision achievable with different unit combinations.
wider: Use combinations in practical tasks: measuring body height in cm and mm
Investigate how digital measurement tools report combinations (e.g. GPS elevation in m and cm)
success_criteria: Student expresses a measurement as a combination of two units correctly
Student explains why a combination provides greater accuracy
